title: Adopted strict-localization model base change on global homology
statement: Let f:X→S be quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism], let s:Spec Ω→S be a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point], and let A be a henselian local ring with separably closed residue field [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. Suppose e:Spec A≅strictLocalization(s), where strictLocalization is the adopted full pointed-affine-neighbourhood model. For maps p:X₀→X and v:X₀→Spec A making a cartesian square over f and e.hom followed by strictLocalizationToBase(s) [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square], every bounded-below derived abelian étale sheaf K and every integer n have invertible global sections on Spec A of Hⁿ of the derived base-change map [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange]. This is the exact fully proved adopted declaration; the small representative-colimit version is the separate node lem-weil-pbc-strict-local-base-change-model-global-homology.

proof.text: The adopted declaration already has a complete kernel-checked proof. Its argument is as follows. On bounded-below injective representatives, the defining factorization of derivedBaseChangeMapPlus identifies it with the derived adjunction mate by uniqueness. The canonical strict-localization mate is invertible after global homology by affine-neighbourhood continuity. Lift X₀ to the canonical pullback; pullback cancellation makes the comparison square cartesian with bottom edge e.hom and hence invertible top edge. Inverse image along these isomorphisms is an exact equivalence preserving injectives, so the factorization on injective representatives proves the comparison-square derived mate invertible. Horizontal pasting expresses the original map as composition isomorphisms, inverse image of the canonical mate, and that comparison mate. Exact inverse image commutes with homology, and global sections after inverse image along e.hom identify with the original sections using the invertible adjunction unit and the direct-image/global-sections composition isomorphism. Thus every factor is invertible after global homology and so is the composite. This node attaches the existing finished library proof; it introduces no unproved step or new Lean declaration.

lean.statement:
theorem isIso_strictHenselization_baseChange_modelGlobalHomology
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f]
    {Ω : Type u} [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (s : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ S)
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [HenselianLocalRing A]
    [IsSepClosed (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A)]
    (eA : Spec (.of A) ≅ strictLocalization s)
    {X₀ : Scheme.{u}} (p₀ : X₀ ⟶ X) (f₀ : X₀ ⟶ Spec (.of A))
    (sq₀ : IsPullback p₀ f₀ f (eA.hom ≫ strictLocalizationToBase s))
    (K : DerivedCategory.Plus (Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}))
    (n : ℤ) :
    IsIso ((Sheaf.Γ (Spec (.of A)).smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}).map
      ((DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor _ n).map
        ((derivedBaseChangeMapPlus AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} sq₀.toCommSq).app K)))
